But now in Christ Jesus, you who once were far off are made near — and the making near happened in blood, which is the one currency that cannot be devalued by your worst week.

So look at the wall. There was a barrier of stone in Jerusalem with a warning carved into it, and every reader of this letter knew what it meant to stand on the wrong side of it. Christ did not cut a door in that wall or issue you a pass. He broke it down in His own flesh and killed the hostility on the cross, and He did it so that He might make of the two one new man — something that did not exist before He made it out of enemies.

You are a fellow citizen now, and more than that, a member of the household. You are a stone being fitted into a temple that God Himself intends to inhabit, and the fitting is not finished. So stop living as though your faith were a private arrangement. Lift your eyes off the ground you were clinging to, look at the men standing in the same wall, and take up your share of the weight.
closingVerse: But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Christ.
carry: Where are you still standing guard over a wall Christ tore down in His own flesh — and what would it cost you to walk through the gap and sit down with the people on the other side?

sections.heading: Where the Dust Lies to You
paras: The book of Acts spends three chapters on the conversion of Saul. On his way to Damascus to hunt Christians, Christ appeared to him and saved him — and made it clear at the same moment that He was setting him aside to carry the gospel to the Gentiles. For a man steeped in the belief that God was concerned chiefly with the Jewish people, that must have landed like a contradiction. Years of study later, Paul came back with a passion for the salvation of the very people he had been raised to keep at a distance.

The dust tells you that your history disqualifies you — that a man with your record may be forgiven but will never be used, that the useful assignments go to men with cleaner files. Psalm 119:25 is the prayer of someone who has believed that and gone quiet: my soul clings to the dust; Revive me according to Your word. (NKJV)

And the reviving word of Ephesians 3 comes from a man in chains who calls himself the very least of all saints and then says that this grace was given to him to preach unsearchable riches. God did not merely forgive the persecutor. He made him the messenger.

sections.heading: A Prisoner of Christ Jesus, Not of Rome
pulls: Rome held the keys, and Paul does not mention Rome. He is not the victim of a legal system. He is the possession of a sovereign Lord, and his chains are an assignment.
paras: Paul opens by naming his circumstances, and the way he names them is the whole lesson: I, Paul, am the prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles. Rome held the keys. Paul does not mention Rome. He is not the victim of an unjust legal system; he is the possession of a sovereign Lord, and his chains are an assignment carried out on somebody’s behalf.

That is not denial. It is a deeper reading of the same facts. The dust reads a hard circumstance as evidence that something has gone wrong. Paul reads it as evidence of who owns him, and then tells the Ephesians not to lose heart over what he is suffering for them, because his suffering is your glory.

parts.label: PART ONE
parts.heading: A MYSTERY THAT IS NO LONGER A SECRET
paras: Paul says that by revelation the mystery was made known to me, and that it in other generations was not made known to the children of men, as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit. You hear the word mystery and think of something unknown. Paul means something that was hidden and has now been told.

So what is it? That the Gentiles are fellow heirs, and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of his promise in Christ Jesus through the Good News. Three compounds in a row, each built on the same prefix: fellow heirs, fellow members, fellow partakers. Not admitted on probation. Not seated at a second table. Joint.

Believing Jew and Gentile have been brought together by Christ to form His church, because Christ, having fulfilled the ceremonial law, has not only reconciled them to God but reconciled them to one another. The mystery was hinted at from the beginning — God told Abraham that in him all the families of the earth would be blessed — but it took the cross to make it plain.

parts.label: PART TWO
parts.heading: THE VERY LEAST OF ALL SAINTS
paras: Then Paul describes himself, and the phrase is remarkable coming from the most effective missionary in history: to me, the very least of all saints, was this grace given. He does not say the least of the apostles here, though he says that elsewhere. He says the least of the saints — the bottom of the whole company of believers.

This is not performance humility. Paul had watched Stephen die and approved of it. He had dragged men and women out of houses. He never lost the memory, and it never crushed him either, because he had learned to hold his record and his commission in the same hand. Was this grace given — the passive verb does all the work. He did not qualify for the assignment. It was handed to him.

And what was he given to preach? The unsearchable riches of Christ. A wealth that cannot be traced out or reached the end of. Paul the persecutor spends his life describing something he will never finish describing.

parts.label: PART THREE
parts.heading: THE CHURCH AS DEMONSTRATION
pulls: God is displaying His wisdom to the powers by means of a congregation of former enemies who have learned to sit together. A divided church obscures the exhibit.
paras: Now Paul says something about the church that most men have never considered. God’s purpose is that now through the assembly the manifold wisdom of God might be made known to the principalities and the powers in the heavenly places.

The audience is not the neighborhood. It is the powers. God is displaying His wisdom to spiritual authorities by means of a mixed congregation of former enemies who have learned to sit together — and the display works precisely because the reconciliation is visible. A divided church is not merely unpleasant. It obscures the exhibit.

The gospel is God’s announcement to a world dead in trespasses and under the control of the prince of the power of the air that Christ has made a way out. It is good news to sinners who justly deserve judgment, not only for their own sin but for their alliance with Adam’s rebellion. And God has entrusted the announcing of it to His church.

parts.label: PART FOUR
parts.heading: BOLDNESS, ACCESS, AND SUFFERING THAT COUNTS
paras: All of it is according to the eternal purpose which he accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord. In him we have boldness and access in confidence through our faith in him. Boldness and access — the freedom to speak plainly and the standing to come in. Both come through Christ, and neither is earned.

Then Paul closes with the pastoral turn: Therefore I ask that you may not lose heart at my troubles for you, which are your glory. He is in prison, and he is worried about their discouragement rather than his own. He wants them to understand that his suffering is not a sign the mission has failed. It is part of how the mission advances.

If you have trusted Christ, you are part of this mysterious church that God is using to carry His once-hidden gospel to every people, language, and nation. Do not let the sin that so easily entangles you, or the ordinary busyness of your life, take your eyes off the work God is continually accomplishing by His Spirit through His church in this world.

stations.verse: How that by revelation the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote before in few words.
stations.question: Do I treat the gospel as a puzzle still being worked out — or as a secret God has deliberately told, and told to me?
stations.gloss: a secret now disclosed; what was hidden and has been told
stations.live: State the gospel in three sentences this week without hedging, out loud, to yourself or to someone else. What God has disclosed plainly, you are allowed to say plainly.
body: Mystērion in Paul is almost the opposite of what the English word suggests. It does not mean a riddle that resists solving. It means something that could not have been worked out by investigation and has now been announced.

That is why Paul can say the mystery was made known and then immediately explain it in a single sentence. A disclosed secret is no longer secret. The only reason anyone knows it is that God decided to say it out loud.

The dust keeps the gospel vague — a spiritual mood, a direction of travel, something you are still piecing together. Mystērion insists it has content, that the content was revealed rather than discovered, and that you are not waiting on further information.

stations.verse: That the Gentiles are fellow heirs, and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of his promise in Christ Jesus through the Good News.
stations.question: Is there anyone in the church I treat as a guest rather than a joint heir — welcome, but not quite family?
stations.gloss: a joint heir; one inheriting equally alongside another
stations.live: Name the believer or the kind of believer you quietly rank below yourself. Then use Paul’s word about him this week, out loud if you can: ‘He is a joint heir with me.’
body: Synklēronomos is the first of three syn- compounds Paul stacks in this verse — joint heirs, joint members, joint partakers. He is hammering the prefix, and the effect in Greek is impossible to miss.
The legal force is precise. A joint heir does not receive a smaller portion or a delayed one. He inherits on the same instrument, at the same time, on the same terms as the one beside him.

The dust always finds a way to rank the room. It grants some believers full membership and gives others a provisional seat. Paul’s three compounds leave no space for tiers. What God gave, He gave jointly.

stations.verse: To me, the very least of all saints, was this grace given, to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ.
stations.question: Do I let my history disqualify me from usefulness — when Paul held his record and his commission in the same hand?
stations.gloss: untraceable; too vast to follow to the end
stations.live: Write down the part of your history you assume disqualifies you. Then write beside it the verb Paul uses: was given. The commission was handed to him, and it was handed to you too.
body: Anexichniastos is built from a negative prefix and ichnos, a footprint. It describes country that cannot be tracked to its border — you may walk into it, but you will never walk out the other side.
Paul uses it only twice, both times of God. In Romans it is God’s ways that cannot be traced out; here it is the riches of Christ. The word is a confession that the subject exceeds the speaker.

Set it next to the phrase before it and the sentence becomes remarkable: the very least of all saints, preaching the untraceable wealth of Christ. The dust says a man’s message is limited by his résumé. Paul’s résumé was persecution, and his subject has no floor.

stations.verse: To the intent that now through the assembly the manifold wisdom of God might be made known to the principalities and the powers in the heavenly places.
stations.question: Do I think of my church as a service I attend — or as the exhibit God is using to display His wisdom to powers I cannot see?
stations.gloss: manifold; of many different colors
stations.live: Look around your congregation this week for one person genuinely unlike you. Sit with him. You are not making conversation — you are part of the pattern being shown to the powers.
body: Polypoikilos occurs only here in the New Testament. Outside the New Testament it described something of many different colors, and Paul applies it to wisdom: wisdom of many colors at once.

The image is deliberate. God’s wisdom is displayed not by a single thread but by a pattern that only appears when unlike threads are woven together — which is exactly what He has done with Jew and Gentile in one body.

So the congregation is the fabric. The dust says church attendance is a private discipline with no audience beyond the room. Paul says the principalities and powers are watching the weave, and every reconciled difference adds a color.

stations.verse: In him we have boldness and access in confidence through our faith in him.
stations.question: Do I come to God carefully, choosing my words to avoid saying the wrong thing — or with the freedom of speech a son actually has?
stations.gloss: boldness; freedom to say everything without concealment
stations.live: Bring God the one thing you have been editing out of your prayers this week. Say it plainly and without softening. The freedom to say everything was bought for you.
body: Parrēsia joins pas, all, to rhēsis, speech — literally all-speech. In ordinary Greek it meant freedom of speech — plainness, openness, nothing held back.
Paul pairs it with access, and the combination is the point: you are brought in, and once inside you may speak without editing. Not merely admitted and expected to keep quiet.

The dust makes a man careful with God. He rehearses, softens, leaves out the parts he is ashamed of, and calls the result reverence. Parrēsia says the freedom to say everything was purchased for you, and using it is not disrespect.

practices.title: NAME THE DISQUALIFICATION
practices.body: Write down the part of your history you assume rules you out of being useful to God. Then write Paul’s verb beside it: was given. He never stopped calling himself the very least of all saints, and he never once used it as a reason to stay quiet.

practices.title: SAY THE MYSTERY PLAINLY
practices.body: State the gospel in three sentences this week, out loud, without hedging. God did not leave it a riddle to be pieced together; He disclosed it on purpose. What He has said plainly, you are permitted to say plainly — and someone in your week needs to hear it in ordinary words.

practices.title: RENAME YOUR CIRCUMSTANCE
practices.body: Paul was held by Rome and called himself the prisoner of Christ Jesus. Take the circumstance you have been describing as an obstacle and describe it once this week the way Paul described his chains — as an assignment, held by Someone who owns you.

practices.title: FIND YOUR UNLIKE BROTHER
practices.body: Look around your congregation for one person genuinely unlike you, and sit with him. God’s manifold wisdom is a many-colored weave, displayed to the powers through unlike threads brought together. You are not being sociable. You are part of the pattern.

practices.title: STOP EDITING YOUR PRAYERS
practices.body: Bring God the thing you have been leaving out — the resentment, the doubt, the sin you keep summarizing rather than naming. You have parrēsia, the freedom of a son to say everything. Using it is not irreverence. Withholding it is not humility.

title: The Mystery Made Known
subtitle: from dust to unsearchable riches
keyVerse: To me, the very least of all saints, was this grace given, to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ.

passage.text: For this cause I, Paul, am the prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles,
if it is so that you have heard of the administration of that grace of God which was given me toward you,
how that by revelation the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote before in few words,
by which, when you read, you can perceive my understanding in the mystery of Christ,
which in other generations was not made known to the children of men, as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit,
that the Gentiles are fellow heirs and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of his promise in Christ Jesus through the Good News,
of which I was made a servant according to the gift of that grace of God which was given me according to the working of his power.
To me, the very least of all saints, was this grace given, to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
and to make all men see what is the administration of the mystery which for ages has been hidden in God, who created all things through Jesus Christ,
to the intent that now through the assembly the manifold wisdom of God might be made known to the principalities and the powers in the heavenly places,
according to the eternal purpose which he accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.
In him we have boldness and access in confidence through our faith in him.
Therefore I ask that you may not lose heart at my troubles for you, which are your glory.

stationsIntro: Read each passage slowly, with your Bible open if you can. Let the verse land first, then answer honestly — and where a Greek word is opened up, let it sharpen the verse you have just prayed over.
lifeIntro: This week is about two things a man tends to hold apart: an honest memory of what he was, and a serious view of what he has been handed. Paul held both in the same sentence and never let go of either.
lifePulls: Do not let the sin that so easily entangles you, or the ordinary busyness of your life, take your eyes off the work God is continually accomplishing by His Spirit through His church.
prayer: Father, You have made known to me a mystery hidden for ages. I was a stranger to Your promises, and You made me a joint heir with Your people. Paul’s history did not stop You from giving him grace, and mine does not stop You either. Thank You for the unsearchable riches of Christ. I have not reached the end of them. Let my church show Your many-sided wisdom by the way unlike men sit together. I have boldness and access to You through faith in Christ; let me use it today. Give me plain words to tell one man the Good News this week. In Jesus’ name, amen.
prayerLines: Father, You have made known to me a mystery hidden for ages.
I was a stranger to Your promises, and You made me a joint heir with Your people.
Paul’s history did not stop You from giving him grace, and mine does not stop You either.
Thank You for the unsearchable riches of Christ. I have not reached the end of them.
Let my church show Your many-sided wisdom by the way unlike men sit together.
I have boldness and access to You through faith in Christ; let me use it today.
Give me plain words to tell one man the Good News this week.
In Jesus’ name, amen.
bottomLine: Paul calls himself the prisoner of Christ Jesus, not of Rome, and tells the secret God has now made plain: the Gentiles are joint heirs, joint members, and joint partakers of the promise in Christ. He calls himself the very least of all saints, and grace was given to him anyway to preach the unsearchable riches of Christ. Your history does not disqualify you. Grace was given to Paul on the same terms it is given to you.
benediction: Lift up your eyes, dusty soul, off the file you keep on yourself and onto the grace that was handed to a man who had hunted the church. Paul never pretended the record was clean. He called himself the very least of all saints and meant it — and in the same breath said that this grace was given to him to preach riches that cannot be traced to their end. He held both, and neither one crushed the other.

The dust told you that a man with your history may be forgiven but will never be used. Look at who is writing. A persecutor in chains, describing his imprisonment as belonging to Christ rather than to Rome, worried not about his own comfort but about whether the Ephesians will lose heart on his account. That is not a man who got over his past. That is a man whose past was swallowed by a commission.

And look at what God is doing with people like you. He is weaving a congregation of former enemies into one body — Jew and Gentile, joint heirs on the same instrument — and He is holding it up before principalities and powers in the heavenly places as the display of His many-colored wisdom. Your church is not a service you attend. It is an exhibit, and you are a thread in it.

So come in with boldness. You have access through Christ and freedom of speech inside the room, and the freedom was purchased so that you would use it. Stop editing your prayers. Stop pricing your usefulness off your worst years. Lift your eyes off the ground you have been clinging to, and go say plainly what God has already said plainly to you.
closingVerse: To me, the very least of all saints, was this grace given, to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ.
carry: Where has your history been functioning as a disqualification — when the man who wrote this letter called himself the very least of all saints and preached unsearchable riches anyway?

sections.heading: Where the Dust Lies to You
paras: One of the hardest things in the Christian life is learning to pray in a biblical way. When someone you love is sick, it is easy to pray. When you see suffering on a screen, it is easy to pray. When you think of a friend who does not know Christ, it is easy to pray. But you sense there has to be more to prayer than the sick, the needy, and the lost.

The dust reduces prayer to a request line for circumstances — a place to file complaints about your situation and hope for a favorable ruling. And when the ruling does not come, prayer quietly stops. Psalm 119:25 is the honest cry of a man who has run out of things to ask for: my soul clings to the dust; Revive me according to Your word. (NKJV)

Paul, writing from prison to people under pressure, prays for none of the things you would have prayed for. Not release. Not relief. Not improved circumstances for anyone. He bows his knees and asks for strength in the inner person, for Christ to dwell in their hearts, for roots in love, for the capacity to comprehend what cannot be measured, and for the fullness of God.

sections.heading: Prayer Built on What God Has Already Done
pulls: Paul does not come to God cold. He prays for this cause — with two chapters of accomplished grace already standing behind the request.
paras: Look at the first three words: For this cause. Paul’s prayer is not free-standing. It grows out of everything he has spent two chapters describing — election before the foundation of the world, redemption in blood, a resurrection out of death, a wall broken down, a temple rising, a mystery disclosed. He does not come to God cold. He comes with the argument already made.

That is the reordering most praying needs. When you come to God asking for help, first remember what He has already done for you in Christ. You are not approaching a stingy Father who dispenses grace in small increments. You are approaching a Father who has already given you more than you could ask or think — and asking Him for what He has shown Himself glad to give.

parts.label: PART ONE
parts.heading: A POSTURE AND A FAMILY NAME
paras: I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named. The standing posture was ordinary for Jewish prayer; kneeling was reserved for moments of unusual weight. Paul is on his knees in a cell.

And the description he gives of the Father is worth slowing over. Every family — every grouping of people who belong to one another, in heaven and on earth — takes its name from Him. Fatherhood is not a human idea projected upward onto God. It is a divine reality that human families are named after.
Which means that whatever your own father was or failed to be, he was a derivative. The original is the One Paul is kneeling in front of.

parts.label: PART TWO
parts.heading: WHAT PAUL ACTUALLY ASKS FOR
paras: The requests come in a chain, each one opening into the next. First: that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person. Not strength to change your circumstances. Strength in the interior life, where no one can see and where everything is finally decided.

Then: that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith. The word for dwell means to settle in as a permanent resident rather than lodge as a guest. Paul is praying that Christ would be at home in them, not visiting.

Then: being rooted and grounded in love, may be strengthened to comprehend with all the saints what is the width and length and height and depth. He mixes a farming word with a building word — roots down, foundation set — and then asks for the ability to take in dimensions he refuses to name the object of. Whatever it is, it runs in every direction at once.

So instead of asking for fortune and relief, learn to ask for strength in the inner person. Rather than asking God to remove your problems and fill your accounts, ask Him to root you and ground you in His love. Instead of asking for wisdom to get you out of holes you dug, ask for the capacity to begin comprehending the love of Christ.

parts.label: PART THREE
parts.heading: TO KNOW WHAT SURPASSES KNOWLEDGE
pulls: There is a knowing that is information and a knowing that is acquaintance. Paul asks for the second, of a love that will always outrun the first.
paras: Then Paul asks for something that sounds like a contradiction: to know Christ’s love which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.

He is not being careless. There is a knowing that is information and a knowing that is acquaintance, and Paul is asking for the second kind of a love that will always exceed the first. You can know a man’s biography exhaustively and not know the man. Paul wants them to know the love, aware the whole time that they will never finish measuring it.

And the outcome he names is larger than any request before it: filled with all the fullness of God. Not filled with information about God. Filled with His fullness — which is either the most reckless sentence in the letter or the truest, and Paul has spent three chapters showing you it is the second.

parts.label: PART FOUR
parts.heading: TO HIM WHO IS ABLE
paras: Then the doxology, and it is one of the great sentences of Scripture: Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us.

Notice where the power is. Not in a distant heaven, waiting to be summoned by sufficiently fervent prayer. According to the power that works in us — already present, already operating. God is able to liberate you from the sin that entangles you. He is able to open the eyes of the lost person you have given up on. He is able to heal the relationships you have written off. And He is able to do it in a way beyond your capacity to imagine in advance.

But Paul understood that when God works, He works for His own glory: to him be the glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen. God’s ability is not a resource you deploy. It is the goodness of a Father who intends to be praised for what He does with people who came to Him empty.

Paul’s example is inspiring, but God’s desire is not that you admire Paul. It is that you ask Him to do a similar work in you. So ask for strength within. Ask for Christ at home in your heart. Ask for roots. And then let Him exceed the request.

stations.verse: From whom every family in heaven and on earth is named.
stations.question: Have I been reading God’s fatherhood through my own father — when Scripture says every family on earth is named after Him, not the reverse?
stations.gloss: a family or lineage descended from one father
stations.live: Name one trait you have unconsciously assigned to God because your father had it. Say the correction out loud: ‘That was a copy, and a poor one. He is the original.’
body: Patria is built directly on patēr, father. It names a group defined by descent from a single head — a clan, a lineage, a household that carries one man’s name.

Paul’s claim is about direction. Every patria in heaven and on earth is named from the Father, which means human fatherhood is the derivative and God’s is the original. You do not scale your father up to imagine Him; He is the pattern every family is a copy of.

The dust runs this backwards. It hands a man his own father’s face and tells him that is what God is like — distant, disappointed, unreliable, or absent. Paul kneels in a prison cell in front of the original.

stations.verse: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person.
stations.question: Am I asking God mainly to change what is around me — when Paul prays for strength in the part of me no one can see?
stations.gloss: to be made strong; to be reinforced with might
stations.live: Ask God this week for strength in the inner person before you ask Him for anything about your circumstances. Then notice how much of your praying has been about the outside.
body: Krataioō comes from kratos, dominion or vigorous strength. It is not the word for enduring a load; it is the word for being made strong. And Paul uses it in the passive — this is strength conferred, not summoned.

The location is what surprises. Not strengthened in circumstances, in health, in resources, or in reputation, but in the inner person — the interior life where a person actually is, and where nobody else can verify the report.

The dust measures a man’s strength by what holds up in public. Paul prays for reinforcement in the one place the public never sees, because that is where every collapse begins long before anyone notices.

stations.verse: That Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love.
stations.question: Is Christ a guest in my life — accommodated in certain rooms — or is He settled in as the resident of the house?
stations.gloss: to settle down and dwell; to reside permanently
stations.live: Name the room you have kept Him out of — the money, the anger, the private appetite, the calendar. Open it this week and say plainly: ‘You live here. It is Your house.’
body: Greek distinguishes between paroikeō, to sojourn as a temporary resident, and katoikeō, to settle in permanently. Paul chooses the second. Christ is not lodging in you; He is taking up residence.
The difference is practical. A guest is given certain rooms and is careful not to rearrange anything. A resident opens every door, throws things out, and changes the house to suit himself over time.

The dust is content with a lodger arrangement. It will happily grant Christ a room — Sunday, the crisis, the part of life already tidy — provided He does not go through the whole house. Katoikeō is a request for exactly that.

stations.verse: May be strengthened to comprehend with all the saints what is the width and length and height and depth.
stations.question: Do I try to understand the love of Christ alone — when Paul says it is grasped with all the saints?
stations.gloss: to seize; to lay hold of and take in fully
stations.live: Ask one other believer this week what he has seen of Christ’s love that you have not. Then listen without correcting. That is what comprehending with all the saints looks like.
body: Katalambanō is stronger than ordinary understanding. It means to seize, to take hold of, to make something your own. Paul uses it elsewhere of pressing on to lay hold of that for which Christ laid hold of him.

But the phrase that governs it is with all the saints. Paul does not pray that they would individually work out the dimensions of Christ’s love. He prays that they would seize it together, because it has four directions and no one stands at more than one corner.
The dust prefers a private spirituality where a man measures God on his own. This verse says the love of Christ is too large for solitary comprehension. You will only ever see your side of it.

stations.verse: Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us.
stations.question: Have my prayers shrunk to the size of what I think is realiztic — and when did I start calling that faith?
stations.gloss: beyond all measure; superabundantly, far past excess
stations.live: Take the prayer you have quietly stopped praying because it seemed unreasonable. Pray it once this week, plainly, and leave the answer with the God whose ability outruns your imagination.
body: Hyperekperissou piles prefixes onto perissos, abundant: hyper, beyond, plus ek, out of, plus abundance. Beyond-out-of-abundantly. English cannot do it without sounding foolish.
The construction is the argument. Paul reaches the edge of ordinary Greek and keeps going, because he is describing a capacity that ordinary language runs out before reaching.

And note the measure he attaches: not above all we ask, but above all we ask or think — past the ceiling of imagination itself. The dust shrinks a man’s prayers to what seems realiztic and calls the shrinkage maturity.

practices.title: PRAY INWARD BEFORE OUTWARD
practices.body: This week, ask God for strength in the inner person before you ask Him for anything about your situation. Keep a rough count of how much of your praying has been about the outside of your life. Paul, in chains, asked for none of it.

practices.title: OPEN THE CLOSED ROOM
practices.body: Christ is not lodging in you; He is taking up residence. Name the room you have kept Him out of — the money, the temper, the private appetite, the calendar you guard. Open it this week and tell Him plainly that the house is His.

practices.title: ASK SOMEONE WHAT HE HAS SEEN
practices.body: The love of Christ has four dimensions and is grasped with all the saints. Ask one other believer this week what he has seen of it that you have not, and listen without improving on his answer. You stand at one corner of something with four.

practices.title: PRAY THE PRAYER YOU GAVE UP ON
practices.body: Find the request you quietly stopped bringing to God because it seemed unrealiztic. Pray it once this week, plainly and without apology. God is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, and the ceiling you installed was yours, not His.

practices.title: CORRECT THE FATHER PICTURE
practices.body: Name one trait you have assigned to God because your own father had it — distance, disappointment, unreliability, silence. Every family on earth is named after Him, not the reverse. Say the correction out loud: that was a copy, and He is the original.

title: Strengthened with Power
subtitle: from dust to the fullness of God
keyVerse: Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us.

passage.text: For this cause, I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named,
that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person,
that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love,
may be strengthened to comprehend with all the saints what is the width and length and height and depth,
and to know Christ’s love which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us,
to him be the glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus to all generations forever and ever. Amen.

stationsIntro: Read each passage slowly, with your Bible open if you can. Let the verse land first, then answer honestly — and where a Greek word is opened up, let it sharpen the verse you have just prayed over.
lifeIntro: This week is about relearning how to pray. Paul is in prison and asks for nothing about his circumstances — and everything about the interior life where a man is actually made or lost.
lifePulls: You are not approaching a stingy Father who dispenses grace in small increments. You are approaching a Father who has already given you more than you could ask or think.
prayer: Father, I bow my knees before You, from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named. Whatever my own father was, You are the original, and You are not rationing Your grace. Strengthen me with power through Your Spirit, in the place no one else can see. Let Christ dwell in my heart through faith — the whole house, not just the rooms I keep tidy. Root me and ground me in love. Let me grasp, with all Your people, a love that surpasses knowledge. You are able to do far more than I ask or think. Teach me to ask. In Jesus’ name, amen.
prayerLines: Father, I bow my knees before You, from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named.
Whatever my own father was, You are the original, and You are not rationing Your grace.
Strengthen me with power through Your Spirit, in the place no one else can see.
Let Christ dwell in my heart through faith — the whole house, not just the rooms I keep tidy.
Root me and ground me in love.
Let me grasp, with all Your people, a love that surpasses knowledge.
You are able to do far more than I ask or think. Teach me to ask.
In Jesus’ name, amen.
bottomLine: Paul kneels in a prison cell and asks for none of the things you would expect — not release, not relief, not easier circumstances for anyone. He asks that they be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person, that Christ would dwell in their hearts, and that they would know a love that surpasses knowledge. Then he closes with the God who is able to do far beyond all you ask or think, by a power already at work in His people.
benediction: Lift up your eyes, dusty soul, off the list of things you have been asking God to fix and onto the Father every family in heaven and on earth is named after. Whatever your own father was or failed to be, he was a copy. The original is the One Paul is kneeling in front of in a prison cell, and He is not distant, not disappointed, and not rationing what He gives.

The dust reduced your praying to circumstances. It made prayer a complaint line, and when the ruling did not come the praying quietly stopped. But look at what Paul asks for on behalf of people who may not survive the year. Not release. Strength in the inner person. Christ settled in the heart as a resident rather than a guest. Roots down into love, and a foundation under it. And then the capacity to take hold, with all the saints, of a love that runs in four directions and will never be finished being measured.

That last request is the one to sit with. To know a love that surpasses knowledge, and to be filled with all the fullness of God — which would be a reckless thing to pray if three chapters had not just shown you a God who chose you before the world, raised you out of a grave, seated you in the heavens, and broke down a wall in His own flesh to get you into the room.

So ask. Ask for strength in the place no one else can see. Ask for Christ at home in the whole house. Ask for roots in a love you will never finish measuring. Ask, because He is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think — not according to your circumstances but according to the power already working in you. Lift your eyes off the ground you are clinging to, and let Him exceed the request.
closingVerse: Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us.
carry: When did your prayers quietly shrink to the size of what seemed realiztic — and what would you ask God for this week if you actually believed He works beyond all you can ask or even think?

sections.heading: Where the Dust Lies to You
paras: Paul has spent three chapters declaring what God has done. He has blessed you with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places. He chose you in Him before the foundation of the world. He predestined you for adoption. He gave you redemption through His blood and the forgiveness of your trespasses. He made you alive together with Christ when you were dead, and raised you, and seated you. He has done a great deal.
Now, in chapter four, it is your turn to respond. And the hinge is the word therefore. In light of everything already given, Paul begs you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called.

The dust hears walk worthily and turns it into a performance review — as though your calling were still pending and your conduct were the evidence being weighed. Psalm 119:25 is the prayer of a man exhausted by that reading: my soul clings to the dust; Revive me according to Your word. (NKJV) But worthiness here is not a qualification you are trying to reach. It is a proportion you are being asked to live in. The calling is already yours.

sections.heading: What a Worthy Walk Looks Like
pulls: The dust hears walk worthily and files it as a performance review. Paul means proportion, not qualification. The calling is already yours; the walking is what fits it.
paras: Paul does not leave it abstract. A worthy walk is one lived with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love, being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. Notice that every item is relational. Not one of them can be practiced alone.

You know you are walking worthily when God by His Spirit is producing that list in you. Remember that the Christian life is not you working up the strength to live for God; it is you dying to your own appetites and asking God, by His Spirit, to live through you. And one of the chief ways that life shows itself is when you take your eyes off yourself and your circumstances and put them on what Christ has accomplished on your behalf.

parts.label: PART ONE
parts.heading: SEVEN THINGS THAT ARE ONE
paras: There is one body and one Spirit, even as you also were called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in us all. Seven ones, driven like nails.

The church is a body, not a collection of independent agents. You need your brothers the way parts of a body need one another. The church confesses that there is no hope outside of Christ, that there is one Lord, and that no other faith or system in this world can rescue a man from his sin and depravity. It confesses one baptism — for as Paul says elsewhere, all who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death and buried with Him, so that they might walk in newness of life.

Believers gather under different denominational names, but these seven are held in common. Only by holding them can the unity of the Spirit be kept in the bond of peace. Note carefully: Paul does not tell you to create unity. He tells you to keep it. The unity already exists because the Spirit made it. Your job is not to build it but to avoid tearing it.

parts.label: PART TWO
parts.heading: THE ASCENDED CHRIST GIVES GIFTS
paras: Then Paul quotes the psalm: When he ascended on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts to people. And he pauses to make sure you notice the shape of it — now this, He ascended, what is it but that he also first descended into the lower parts of the earth? He who descended is the one who also ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things.

Down first, then up. Christ went to the lowest place before He took the highest, and the gifts He distributes now are distributed by a Man who has been to the bottom of the dust and come out above every heaven. That is who is handing out assignments in your church.

And what did He give? Some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers. Apostles: sent ones, spokesmen who speak with authority. Prophets: the gift of clear, forceful proclamation of the word of God. Evangelists: those who carry the good news outward. Shepherds and teachers: the gift of feeding and guarding the flock of God.

parts.label: PART THREE
parts.heading: WHAT THE GIFTS ARE FOR
pulls: The gifted men were given to equip the saints for the work of service. The leaders are not the workers. They are the ones who put tools in your hands.
paras: Here is the sentence that should reorganize how you think about church: the gifted men were given for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving, to the building up of the body of Christ. The leaders are not the workers. The leaders are the equippers, and the saints do the work of service.

The goal is stated plainly: until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a full grown man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ. Not until the building is full. Not until the budget clears. Until the body reaches maturity measured by Christ Himself.

While much of the church today measures success by numbers, Paul is calling for unity and knowledge. There are congregations with the numbers on their side that promote discord rather than unity. And for the knowledge of the Son of God to take root, the whole counsel of Scripture must be preached — which is harder to find than it should be.

parts.label: PART FOUR
parts.heading: NO LONGER CHILDREN
paras: Paul then describes what immaturity looks like: that we may no longer be children, tossed back and forth and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, in craftiness, after the wiles of error. A spiritual child is not innocent; he is unstable. He moves with whatever is currently blowing, and he is available to anyone with a persuasive line.

The remedy is not merely more information. It is speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him who is the head, Christ. Truth and love together — the two things men are forever pitting against each other. When you hear that a man is too concerned with truth, or too concerned with love, the criticizm is misguided. Be concerned that the truth of God is preserved and that the love of Christ is shown, and stand firmly for both.

Then the body image again: from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love. Just as joints and ligaments and muscles work together to make a physical body function, so the body of Christ must work. This should free you from treating your faith as an independent pursuit of God and let you see that you are a part, and that your part is necessary.

When the saints are properly equipped and know what the Scriptures teach, they can stand firm and proclaim Christ in the middle of difficulty, opposition, and deceit. Their lives will not rise and fall with the culture. They will stand, with their eyes fixed on Jesus, the author and perfecter of their faith.

stations.verse: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called.
stations.question: Am I trying to become worthy of my calling — or learning to live in proportion to a calling I already have?
stations.gloss: worthily; in a way that balances the weight of something
stations.live: Before one hard conversation or decision this week, ask a different question than usual. Not ‘am I good enough for this?’ but ‘what would match the weight of what God has already given me?’
body: Axiōs comes from axios, which originally described the balancing of scales — a weight matching what was set opposite it. To live axiōs of something is to live at the same weight as the thing itself.

That kills the performance reading immediately. Paul is not asking you to earn the calling; the calling has already been placed on the scale by God. He is asking you to bring a life over that corresponds to it.

The dust turns every imperative into a qualification. Axiōs keeps the order Paul has kept for three chapters: the indicative first, the command standing on top of it. You are not walking toward the calling. You are walking under it.

stations.verse: Being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
stations.question: Do I think of unity as something the church has to build — or as something the Spirit already made that I am charged with guarding?
stations.gloss: to guard; to keep watch over something already possessed
stations.live: Name the relationship in your church you have let quietly lapse. You are not being asked to build unity there — only to stop damaging what the Spirit already made. Make one contact this week.
body: Tēreō is a watchman’s word. It means to keep by guarding — to preserve what is already in hand. It does not mean to create, produce, or negotiate into being.

So the unity in question is not a project. It is the unity of the Spirit, made by God when He put believers into one body, and Paul’s instruction is that you be diligent not to damage what He has already joined.

The dust reframes this as consensus-building, which conveniently makes unity conditional on everyone agreeing with you. Tēreō says the unity is a fact you are standing guard over, and the only question is whether you are guarding it or breaching it.

stations.verse: For the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving, to the building up of the body of Christ.
stations.question: Do I go to church to receive a service — or to be equipped for work that is mine to do?
stations.gloss: equipping; setting something in working order
stations.live: Ask yourself honestly what you were equipped for last Sunday, and then do one thing with it this week. A net that is mended and never cast has not been put in working order.
body: Katartismos appears only here in the New Testament. It comes from katartizō, the verb Matthew uses for James and John mending their nets and Paul uses for restoring a brother caught in a fault. Both pictures carry the same idea: taking something that cannot presently do its job and putting it into working condition.
Which tells you what the gifted men are for. They are not hired to do the ministry while the congregation watches. They exist to mend the saints so the saints can work.

The dust prefers a church of spectators, because a spectator is never responsible and never exposed. Katartismos assumes you are a net that is meant to be fishing, and the preaching you sit under is the mending.

stations.verse: That we may no longer be children, tossed back and forth and carried about with every wind of doctrine.
stations.question: Where am I still unstable — moving with whatever is currently persuasive rather than standing on what I know is true?
stations.gloss: to be tossed by waves; to surge back and forth
stations.live: Name one conviction you have quietly softened because holding it became socially expensive. Take it back to Scripture this week and decide whether you drift or stand.
body: Klydōnizō appears only here in the New Testament. It comes from klydōn, a surge of the sea — the word James uses for the doubter, like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed. It describes a small craft at the mercy of water — not sinking, but with no say in where it goes.
Paul pairs it with a second image, being carried about by wind, so the picture is a boat pushed by sea and sky at once. That is his definition of spiritual childhood: not innocence but instability.

The dust flatters this as open-mindedness. But a man who moves with every persuasive wind is not open; he is available, and Paul says the men working the wind know exactly what they are doing. Maturity is having somewhere to stand.

stations.verse: But speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him who is the head, Christ.
stations.question: Which do I habitually sacrifice — the truth to keep the peace, or the love to make the point?
stations.gloss: to be truthful; to deal in truth, not merely to state it
stations.live: Identify the conversation you have been avoiding. Do not choose between honesty and kindness this week — plan how to bring both into the same sentence, and then have it.
body: Alētheuō is a verb, not a noun — literally to truth. It is broader than saying true things; it means dealing truthfully, living without pretence, being a man whose words and life are not two different reports.
Paul attaches in love, and the pairing is the whole point. Truth without love becomes a weapon, and love without truth becomes flattery. The church matures on both or on neither.

The dust always offers a trade. Keep the peace and shave the truth, or make the point and spend the relationship. Whenever you hear a man criticized for caring too much about one of them, the criticizm itself is the tell.

practices.title: CHANGE THE QUESTION
practices.body: Before your next hard decision, stop asking whether you are good enough for it. Ask instead what would match the weight of what God has already given you. Worthiness here is proportion, not qualification — the calling is already on the scale.

practices.title: GUARD, DO NOT BUILD
practices.body: You are told to keep the unity of the Spirit, not manufacture it. Name the relationship in your church you have let quietly lapse, and make one contact this week. You are not being asked to create anything. Only to stop damaging what God already joined.

practices.title: CAST THE NET
practices.body: The gifted men exist to mend and set you for work that is yours. Ask honestly what you were equipped for the last time you sat under preaching, and then do one thing with it before Sunday. A net that is mended and never cast has not been put in working order.

practices.title: TAKE BACK THE SOFTENED CONVICTION
practices.body: A spiritual child is not innocent; he is unstable, moving with whatever wind is currently blowing. Name one thing you have quietly softened because holding it became costly. Take it back to Scripture this week and decide whether you drift or stand.

practices.title: REFUSE THE TRADE
practices.body: Identify the conversation you have been avoiding, and refuse the choice between honesty and kindness. Plan how to get truth and love into the same sentence, and then have the conversation. The body grows up on both together, not on one at the expense of the other.

title: Walk Worthy, Grow Up
subtitle: from dust to the measure of Christ
keyVerse: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called.

passage.text: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, even as you also were called in one hope of your calling,
one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all, and in us all.
But to each one of us, the grace was given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
Therefore he says, “When he ascended on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts to people.”
Now this, “He ascended”, what is it but that he also first descended into the lower parts of the earth?
He who descended is the one who also ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things.
He gave some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers;
for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving, to the building up of the body of Christ,
until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a full grown man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ,
that we may no longer be children, tossed back and forth and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, in craftiness, after the wiles of error;
but speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him who is the head, Christ,

from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.

stationsIntro: Read each passage slowly, with your Bible open if you can. Let the verse land first, then answer honestly — and where a Greek word is opened up, let it sharpen the verse you have just prayed over.
lifeIntro: This week turns the corner from what God has done to how a man responds. Everything Paul asks for here is relational — none of it can be practiced alone, and none of it earns the calling it answers.
lifePulls: The Christian life is not you working up the strength to live for God. It is you dying to your own appetites and asking God, by His Spirit, to live through you.
prayer: Father, You called me before I ever walked a step for You. Make my walk match the weight of that calling — not to earn it, but because it is already mine. Give me lowliness, humility, and patience with the men I find hard to bear. Show me where I am damaging the unity Your Spirit made, and stop me. Thank You for one Lord, one faith, one baptism, and one Father over all. Equip me through Your word for the work You have given me. Grow me up into Christ, my head, by speaking truth in love. In Jesus’ name, amen.
prayerLines: Father, You called me before I ever walked a step for You.
Make my walk match the weight of that calling — not to earn it, but because it is already mine.
Give me lowliness, humility, and patience with the men I find hard to bear.
Show me where I am damaging the unity Your Spirit made, and stop me.
Thank You for one Lord, one faith, one baptism, and one Father over all.
Equip me through Your word for the work You have given me.
Grow me up into Christ, my head, by speaking truth in love.
In Jesus’ name, amen.
bottomLine: After three chapters of what God has done, Paul writes therefore and asks for a walk that matches the weight of the calling: lowliness, humility, patience, and diligence to keep a unity the Spirit already made. The ascended Christ gives gifted men to equip the saints for the work of service, not to do it while the saints watch. The goal is a grown man, measured by the fullness of Christ, no longer tossed by every wind of doctrine, growing up into the Head by speaking truth in love.
benediction: Lift up your eyes, dusty soul, off the performance review you have been running on yourself and onto the calling that was placed on you before you did anything about it. Paul says walk worthily, and the dust hears a standard you are failing. He means a balance — a life brought over to match a weight God has already set on the scale. You are not walking toward the calling. You are walking under it.

And look at what that walk is made of. Not achievement. Lowliness, humility, patience, bearing with one another in love, and a stubborn diligence to guard the unity the Spirit has already made. Every one of them is relational, and not one can be practiced by a man alone in a room. This is the part of the Christian life that cannot be done privately, which is exactly why the dust keeps recommending that you try.

So look at who is handing out the assignments. The One who descended into the lower parts of the earth before He ascended far above all the heavens — the Christ who went to the bottom of your dust and came out over every power that ever frightened you. He gives shepherds and teachers, and He gives them to mend you, the way a man mends a net, so that you can work.

Grow up, then. Not tossed by every wind that blows through your feed and your circle, but speaking truth in love and increasing into the Head. You are a joint in a body, fitted and knit together, and the body builds itself up in love only as each part does its work. Lift your eyes off the ground you are clinging to, and take your place in the frame.
closingVerse: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called.
carry: Where have you been sitting as a spectator in a body that needs you as a working joint — and what were you equipped for last Sunday that you have not yet done anything with?

sections.heading: Where the Dust Lies to You
paras: The body grows when its members are speaking truth in love and growing up in every way into Christ, who is the head. Through the equipping of the church you are established in both truth and love. Whenever you hear people pitting truth against love, or love against truth, you can be confident they have not understood what the Bible teaches about either. They are not opponents. They are companions in the growth of Christian maturity.
And these words are not written for you to apply in isolation. They are written for the whole church to apply together, so that you grow up with your brothers as one body into Him who is the head.

The dust tells you that change is a matter of willpower applied consistently — that if you were serious enough, the old patterns would fall away. Then, when they do not, it tells you that you are simply the kind of man who cannot change. Psalm 119:25 is the prayer of someone caught between those two lies: my soul clings to the dust; Revive me according to Your word. (NKJV)

sections.heading: Why Change Is So Hard
pulls: The dust offers two lies in sequence: that willpower will fix you, and then that nothing will. Paul offers a third thing — an old man to take off and a new man to put on.
paras: The reason change is difficult is that most of the sinful habits ruling you were inherited. When sin entered the world at the fall, it passed from generation to generation, and you were born with the tendencies and appetites of those who came before you. Outside of God’s intervention in Christ, they will govern you until you die. Because there is none who does good, not even one, nothing you inherited by nature brings glory to God.

So Paul does not hand you a technique. He hands you three verbs, and they are all in the passive or the middle where it counts: put off, be renewed, put on. Something is done to you before anything is required of you, and what is required of you flows out of it.

parts.label: PART ONE
parts.heading: THE FUTILITY YOU CAME OUT OF
paras: Paul’s first command is that you no longer walk as the rest of the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their mind. The word for futility means emptiness — activity that produces nothing that lasts. You are no longer to live in futility as you once did, because those who were dead in trespasses and sins have been made alive in Christ.

Then he traces where futility goes if it is left alone: being darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the hardening of their hearts. They, having become callous, gave themselves up to lust, to work all uncleanness with greediness.

Read that chain slowly, because it is a progression, not a list. Futility darkens understanding. Darkened understanding alienates. Alienation hardens. Hardness produces callousness — and a callus is not an injury, it is a protection the body builds where there has been repeated friction. That is the frightening part. If you are not growing up together in Christ in truth and love, you will grow numb toward the things of God and never feel it happening. You know you are walking in futility when your desire for God’s glory is thinning and your appetite for your own agenda is growing.

parts.label: PART TWO
parts.heading: BUT THAT IS NOT HOW YOU LEARNED CHRIST
paras: Then Paul breaks the chain with a sentence that ought to be underlined: But you didn’t learn Christ that way. Whatever you absorbed about how life works before you knew Him, it did not come from Him, and it does not have to keep instructing you.

And here come the three verbs. That you put away, as concerning your former way of life, the old man that grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit; and that you be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man, who in the likeness of God has been created in righteousness and holiness of truth.

Notice the order. Take off, be renewed, put on — and the renewal sits in the middle, in the spirit of your mind, because clothing changes are not enough if the man wearing them thinks the same way he always did. Also notice what the old self is doing: it grows corrupt, present tense, continuously. It is not stable. Left alone it rots, which is precisely why putting it off is not optional maintenance.

Because of the finished work of Christ, because of the power of the Spirit working mightily within you, and because God Himself is always willing and working for His good pleasure in your life, there is hope. If God has exposed something in you today, ask Him for the strength to take off the old corrupt self with its deceitful desires, and to put on the new.

parts.label: PART THREE
parts.heading: WHAT COMES OFF AND WHAT GOES ON
pulls: Repentance is not merely stopping a sin. Watch the thief: from taking, to working, to giving. He is turned all the way around until he is doing the opposite.
paras: Paul then gets specific, and the pattern is always the same: not merely stop, but replace. Put away lying, and speak truth each one with his neighbor, for we are members of one another. The reason given is not that lying is impolite but that you and your brothers are parts of the same body, and a body that misreports its own condition cannot be treated.

Be angry, and don’t sin. Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath, and don’t give place to the devil. Paul is not saying anger is never appropriate. He is warning that anger left overnight becomes an opening — a place given, a foothold offered.

Let him who stole steal no more; but rather let him labor, producing with his hands something that is good, that he may have something to give to him who has need. Watch the full arc: from taking, to working, to giving. Repentance is not merely stopping a sin. It is being turned all the way around until you are doing the opposite.

Then the speech: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear. And the warning that follows is one of the most personal in the letter: don’t grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. The Spirit who marked you as God’s own possession is a Person, and He can be grieved — not by strangers, but by you.

parts.label: PART FOUR
parts.heading: FORGIVE AS YOU WERE FORGIVEN
paras: The final list comes off in one motion: let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander be put away from you, with all malice. And then the replacement: be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.

That last clause is the standard and the supply at once. You are not asked to generate forgiveness out of your own reserves of patience. You are asked to hand on what was handed to you — and you have already been shown, in chapter two, exactly how much that was.

The good news of the gospel is not do this and you will live, but because Christ has done everything necessary to save you, through faith in Him you can live. If the good news were do this and live, you would be lost. Everyone who turns away from himself — from his good works and his bad ones alike — and looks to Christ as He is offered in the gospel is credited with Christ’s righteousness and saved.

So walk in a manner worthy of your calling. Stop lying. Do not let anger rule you. Stop taking what is not yours. God has promised to supply what you need, so work diligently and let Him provide. Remember: it is not by doing these things that you are justified. It is that those who have been justified are now free to stop doing them.

stations.verse: That you no longer walk as the rest of the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their mind.
stations.question: Where am I spending real effort on something that will produce nothing that lasts — and calling it a full life?
stations.gloss: futility; emptiness that yields no result
stations.live: Look at your calendar for last week and mark the hours honestly: which of them produced something that will still matter in ten years? Do not resolve to fix it all — change one block.
body: Mataiotēs describes something that fails to achieve its purpose — effort without yield. It is the word the Greek Old Testament uses for the great refrain of Ecclesiastes: vanity, vapor, breath.
Paul locates it in the mind rather than the behavior. Futility is not primarily what these men do; it is how they think, and the emptiness of the output traces back to the emptiness of the reasoning.
The dust is content for you to be busy, respectable, and productive, so long as none of it lasts. That is the version of a wasted life nobody notices, including the man living it.

stations.verse: They, having become callous, gave themselves up to lust, to work all uncleanness with greediness.
stations.question: Where have I gone numb — not shocked by something that would have grieved me five years ago?
stations.gloss: to stop feeling pain; to become past feeling
stations.live: Name one thing that once troubled your conscience and no longer does. Do not argue about whether it should. Take it to God this week and ask Him to restore the feeling.
body: Apalgeō occurs only here in the New Testament. It joins a prefix meaning away from to algeō, to feel pain — literally, to have ceased hurting. Physicians used related language for a limb that no longer registered sensation.

That is Paul’s diagnosis of hardened sin, and it explains why it is so difficult to detect from the inside. The problem is not that the conscience is screaming and being ignored. The problem is that it has gone quiet.
The dust calls this maturity — you have simply grown less easily shocked. But losing the ability to feel pain is not strength. It is how a man walks on a broken foot until the bone gives way.

stations.verse: And that you be renewed in the spirit of your mind.
stations.question: Am I trying to change my behavior while leaving the way I think about God, myself, and my sin exactly as it was?
stations.gloss: to be made new again; renewed continuously
stations.live: Name one belief about yourself that survived your conversion untouched — about your worth, your anger, or what you deserve. Bring it into the light this week and ask what Scripture actually says.
body: Ananeoomai appears only here in the New Testament. It is passive and, in Greek, continuous — be being renewed. You are not the agent, and the work is not finished in a single stroke. Something is being done to you, and it keeps being done.
Its position matters as much as its meaning. Paul puts renewal between putting off and putting on, because a change of clothes does not help a man who still thinks the way he did in the old ones.

The dust is happy to negotiate about behavior, which can be managed in public, so long as the mind underneath stays untouched. Ananeoomai goes for the mind — and puts God, not your discipline, in charge of the renovation.

stations.verse: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
stations.question: Does my speech leave people built up — or does it mostly leave them informed of my opinion?
stations.gloss: rotten; spoiled and unfit for use
stations.live: Replay one thing you said this week that was accurate but corrosive. Do not merely resolve to be nicer — go back and say the version that would have given grace.
body: Sapros is the word for rotten fruit and for fish thrown away as spoiled. It does not mean vulgar. It means decayed — something that was once good and has gone off, and now contaminates whatever it touches.
So Paul is not merely banning coarse language. He is describing speech that has rotted: the corrosive remark, the accurate criticizm delivered to wound, the true thing said to diminish.

And the replacement is a test, not a rule. Did it build up as the need required? Did it give grace to the people who heard it? The dust lets a man defend a rotten sentence on the grounds that it was true.

stations.verse: Don’t grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
stations.question: Do I think of my sin as breaking rules — or as wounding a Person who lives in me and will not leave?
stations.gloss: to grieve; to cause sorrow to someone who loves you
stations.live: Name the sin you have been treating as a rule you broke. Confess it this week as what Paul calls it — grief caused to Someone who sealed you and has not left.
body: Lypeō means to cause grief, and it is a word reserved for persons. You can damage a thing, but you cannot grieve it. Paul has deliberately chosen relational vocabulary for what sin does to God’s Spirit.
Note carefully what he does not say. He does not say the Spirit will leave — in the same breath he says in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. The seal is not in question. The sorrow is.

The dust offers two errors, and both are easier than the truth. Either sin is rule-breaking with no personal weight, or it is so serious that the Spirit withdraws. Lypeō says He stays, and He grieves.

practices.title: AUDIT ONE WEEK OF FUTILITY
practices.body: Look back at your calendar and mark honestly which hours produced something that will still matter in ten years. Do not resolve to overhaul everything — that resolution never survives Wednesday. Change one block this week and let it hold.

practices.title: FIND WHERE YOU WENT NUMB
practices.body: Name one thing that troubled your conscience five years ago and no longer does. Do not argue about whether it should. A callus is not an injury; it is protection built where there has been repeated friction. Ask God this week to restore the feeling.

practices.title: REPLACE, DO NOT JUST STOP
practices.body: Follow the thief through the verse: he stops stealing, he works with his hands, and he ends up with something to give away. Take one sin you are trying to quit and name its opposite. Then do the opposite this week instead of merely resisting.

practices.title: GO BACK AND SAY IT RIGHT
practices.body: Replay one thing you said this week that was accurate but corrosive. Paul’s test is not whether it was true but whether it built up and gave grace to those who heard it. Go back and say the version that would have.

practices.title: CONFESS IT AS GRIEF
practices.body: Take the sin you have been treating as a broken rule and confess it as Paul frames it — sorrow caused to the Holy Spirit, who sealed you for the day of redemption and has not left. He is a Person, not a policy, and He stayed.

title: Put Off, Be Renewed, Put On
subtitle: from dust to the new self
keyVerse: That you put away, as concerning your former way of life, the old man that grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit; and that you be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man.

passage.text: This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that you no longer walk as the rest of the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their mind,
being darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the hardening of their hearts.
They, having become callous, gave themselves up to lust, to work all uncleanness with greediness.
But you didn’t learn Christ that way,
if indeed you heard him, and were taught in him, even as truth is in Jesus:
that you put away, as concerning your former way of life, the old man that grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit,
and that you be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
and put on the new man, who in the likeness of God has been created in righteousness and holiness of truth.
Therefore putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor. For we are members of one another.
“Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath,
and don’t give place to the devil.
Let him who stole steal no more; but rather let him labor, producing with his hands something that is good, that he may have something to give to him who has need.
Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
Don’t grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander be put away from you, with all malice.
And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.

stationsLabel: THE WORD ON THE NEW MAN
stationsIntro: Read each passage slowly, with your Bible open if you can. Let the verse land first, then answer honestly — and where a Greek word is opened up, let it sharpen the verse you have just prayed over.
lifeIntro: This week is about three verbs and their order: put off, be renewed, put on. Change is not willpower applied to behavior. It is a change of clothes made possible by a change of mind, worked by Someone else.
lifePulls: It is not by doing these things that you are justified. It is that those who have been justified are now free to stop doing them.
prayer: Father, I did not learn Christ the way I learned the world. Show me what is still on me from the old life. I would rather see it than defend it. The old man is rotting, and I cannot repair him; help me put him off. Renew the spirit of my mind, not just my behavior. Clothe me in the new man You created in righteousness and holiness. Guard my mouth from rotten words, and let my speech give grace to those who hear. Keep me from grieving Your Holy Spirit, in whom I was sealed. Teach me to forgive as You forgave me in Christ. In Jesus’ name, amen.
prayerLines: Father, I did not learn Christ the way I learned the world.
Show me what is still on me from the old life. I would rather see it than defend it.
The old man is rotting, and I cannot repair him; help me put him off.
Renew the spirit of my mind, not just my behavior.
Clothe me in the new man You created in righteousness and holiness.
Guard my mouth from rotten words, and let my speech give grace to those who hear.
Keep me from grieving Your Holy Spirit, in whom I was sealed.
Teach me to forgive as You forgave me in Christ.
In Jesus’ name, amen.
bottomLine: Paul traces where futility goes if it is left alone — darkened understanding, alienation from God, and finally a callus that feels nothing. Then he breaks the chain: But you didn’t learn Christ that way. Put off the old man, be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man created in God’s likeness. Then forgive as God in Christ forgave you, handing on what was handed to you.
benediction: Lift up your eyes, dusty soul, off the failed resolutions stacked behind you and onto the new man God has already created in righteousness and holiness of truth. You have tried willpower and it did not hold, and then the dust told you the honest conclusion was that you are simply the kind of man who does not change. Paul offers a third thing, and it is not a technique. It is a wardrobe.

But hear the warning underneath first, because it is the mercy in this passage. Futility darkens the understanding, and darkened understanding alienates, and alienation hardens, and hardness ends in a callus — a place that has stopped feeling anything at all. That is not a dramatic collapse. It is the quietest thing that can happen to a man, and he is the last to know. If something in you has gone numb, the fact that you can still feel the numbness is grace.

So look at the sentence that breaks the chain. But you didn’t learn Christ that way.
